key_insight: This paper compiles and synthesizes explainable AI techniques adapted to protein language models, clarifying how different methods reveal sequence–structure–function relationships and where current approaches succeed or fall short.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap in understanding and trusting protein language model predictions by surveying XAI methods, identifying applicability to biological questions, and highlighting evaluation gaps and best practices for interpretation.
method: Systematic survey and taxonomy of XAI techniques applied to protein LMs (e.g., attribution, probing, attention analysis, representation visualization).
Mapping of methods to protein-specific modalities and tasks (sequence signals, structural contexts, functional annotations) and discussion of adaptations needed.
Critical comparison of strengths, limitations, evaluation metrics, and recommended workflows for practitioners interpreting model outputs.
impact: Provides researchers and ML practitioners a practical roadmap to interpret and validate protein LM outputs, improving trust, hypothesis generation, and safer use in protein design and biological discovery.
visual_elements: Taxonomy diagram grouping XAI methods by approach and typical biological question addressed.
Flowchart mapping methods to concrete use-cases (structure prediction, mutation effect, functional annotation).
Sequence heatmap / attention or attribution overlay with a 3D protein structure inset to show biological relevance.
Comparison chart/table of methods vs. evaluation metrics, interpretability strength, and computational cost.
paper_title: Towards the explainability of protein language models
